title: runtime-speculative-handshake-model-routing-with-acceptance-calibration-and-degraded-mode-plan
creator: Priya Raman
description: Draft plan for integrating a lightweight speculative handshake between the router and decoder to enable fast-path routing to lower-cost model variants with calibrated acceptance metrics and a transparent degraded-mode fallback. This work bridges kernel-aware routing, attention optimization signals and prefill/decode scheduling in the serving runtime. Goal: reduce average token cost while keeping 99th percentile latency and quality regression within tolerances.
acceptance_criteria: Router can execute a 2-step speculative handshake: (1) prefill probe on candidate model variants and (2) acceptance scoring response within configured budget (CPU/GPU ms)
Acceptance metric computed per-request (normalized acceptance score) and stored in telemetry for SLO/alerting
Automatic fallback to full-precision or primary model variant when acceptance_score < threshold or probe timeout occurs
No regression > 1% absolute BLEU/ROUGE-equivalent on representative prompt set under canary traffic
End-to-end P50/P95 latency for canary traffic does not increase by > 5% vs baseline when handshake enabled for < 10% of requests
implementation_notes: Design emphasizes minimal runtime changes to decoder hot path: prefill probe should be performed by a non-blocking kernel path that computes a small set of features (entropy, top-k mass, next-token logits projection) without committing long-lived KV state unless accepted. Kernel selection hints flow from router to decoder: prefer quantized F16/INT8 kernels for probe; if probe acceptance is positive, attach KV snapshot or warm-up token sequence to shorten subsequent decode. Use attention-optimized kernels (block-sparse for long context) during probe when context length > 1024 to get realistic acceptance signal. Probe budget defaults: 6ms on A100-equivalent, 12ms on T4-equivalent. Probe size: 8 tokens of simulated decode (configurable).
tradeoffs_and_risks: Extra compute from probes increases tail-load; mitigate with sampling policy (user-tier, request-size, route) and cache probe results per prompt fingerprint
Probes may bias acceptance metrics for certain prompt distributions; plan includes offline calibration runs across corpora and per-customer thresholds
KV snapshot/transfer introduces memory churn; implement soft-attached KV references and GC after commit to accepted decode
Kernel hinting may increase heterogeneity; ensure runtime kernel-capability table is consulted to avoid scheduling to incompatible nodes
telemetry_and_metrics: Track these as time-series and histograms: acceptance_score (0..1), probe_latency_ms, probe_success_rate, early_accept_rate, fallback_rate, end2end_latency_p50/p95/p99, token_cost_delta, quality_regression_metric on canary prompt set. Alert if fallback_rate > 5% for 1h or quality_regression_metric exceeds threshold. Create dashboard with per-model, per-kernel, per-region breakdowns.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag gated implementation on runtime branch; 2) Internal canary: 1% synthetic traffic for 48h, validate metrics; 3) Dev customers: 5% segmented by non-critical tenants for 7 days; 4) Gradual ramp to 25% while adjusting acceptance thresholds; 5) Full rollout with opt-in for P0 tiers until SLOs stable. Include kill-switch circuit-breaker based on fallback/latency triggers.
